item: The backup route's Origin/Referer check is the POST middleware's own _foreign_origin, so a proxy's Host NAME:443 with Origin https://NAME is the same server
summary: GET /api/database/backup refused for itself the requests another site makes (A-008) and compared the sent Origin (else Referer) with the request's Host header as raw strings: behind a TLS-terminating proxy that hands the app Host 'oo.lan:443' while the browser sends Origin 'https://oo.lan', the pair is the same server but the strings differ, so the app's own page was refused. RC2's #1538 added the normaliser the POST middleware uses (_foreign_origin: scheme-default ports normalised, the hostname must be one the app serves, another port is another origin, Origin: null refused) and src/api/cross_site.py's refuse_cross_site_get already uses it; the route now calls it too (the Host check and the Sec-Fetch-Site check are unchanged, the 403 text is unchanged, the unused urlsplit import is gone). One test with the proxy pair in both spellings (Host oo.lan:443 with Origin https://oo.lan, a Referer, and Host oo.lan with Origin http://oo.lan:80) and four foreigners (another host, another port, the other scheme's default port, null); 3 mutants caught (the old raw compare, a hostname-only compare, never foreign), and the existing foreign-origin tests of the file pass unchanged (69). Stated: behind a proxy that strips the port from Host (Host 'oo.lan') while the app sees http, the Origin https://oo.lan is still read as port 443 against 80, the middleware's existing decision, not changed here; the stale sentence in src/api/cross_site.py's docstring ('is to be pointed here later') is RC2's file and is left for them.
